entrypoints.summary: A user submits blob data through Put(); the finding describes handling PUT requests and shows Server.handlePostShared reading the HTTP request body.

affected_components.role: The report's vulnerable request-body read and subsequent encoding path.

causal_paths.kind: HTTP blob body to unbounded read and encoding

code_slices.fixed: The report recommends assigning r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, MaxAllowedEncodedBlobSize) before io.ReadAll and returning HTTP 413 for an oversized body.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The report derives MaxAllowedBlobSize from MaxSRSPoints, BytesPerSymbol, and MaxCodingRatio, and says to reserve an encoding-expansion buffer.
code_slices.vulnerable: Server.handlePostShared calls io.ReadAll(r.Body) without a body-size limit; the finding states the body data is then passed to EncodeBlob.

relation_candidates.rationale: The report states that user-submitted blob data is carried in an HTTP body with no size limit and is read by io.ReadAll.
The report says that data read through io.ReadAll is subsequently passed to EncodeBlob.
EDAP-02 characterizes the unbounded read and subsequent processing as leading to resource-exhaustion DoS, while qualifying resource-dependent practicality.
The report recommends http.MaxBytesReader with MaxAllowedEncodedBlobSize before io.ReadAll to impose the ingress bound.

impact.affected_asset: Availability of the EigenDA Proxy service
impact.attacker_capability: Cause the proxy to fully read and process an arbitrarily large HTTP blob body, subject to deployment resource constraints.

causal_trace.summary: A user-controlled blob is supplied in an HTTP request body through the proxy's Put request path.
The request body has no enforced ingress size limit despite the report-defined EigenDA maximum blob size, with an allowance needed for encoding inefficiency.
Server.handlePostShared invokes io.ReadAll(r.Body) on the unbounded body; the report states the resulting data is then passed to e.client.GetCodec().EncodeBlob(value).
Reading and processing arbitrary-sized supplied data can exhaust proxy resources and cause denial of service; practical exploitation depends on network, CPU, and memory conditions.

failure.operation: Unbounded io.ReadAll(r.Body) followed by blob encoding in Server.handlePostShared.

primary_invariant.statement: Accepted user-supplied blob input must not exceed MaxAllowedBlobSize = uint64(MaxSRSPoints * BytesPerSymbol / MaxCodingRatio), adjusted for encoding expansion, before it is fully read and encoded.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The handler reads r.Body with io.ReadAll without first applying a bound derived from the allowed encoded blob size.

quality.review_notes: The primary audit report directly provides the vulnerable handler excerpt, protocol-size formula, bounded-reader recommendation, and states that PR #277 implemented the recommendation. The bundle contains neither the PR/patch nor a source revision, test, runtime trace, or resource-consumption measurement; implementation details, rejection behavior in deployed code, and quantitative reproducibility remain unverified.

remediation.invariant_restored: Wrap r.Body with http.MaxBytesReader using MaxAllowedEncodedBlobSize before io.ReadAll, so ingress is limited to the protocol-derived bound plus encoding allowance; the report's example returns HTTP 413 when the read fails for excessive size.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Submit a blob request whose body exceeds the protocol-derived blob-size bound.
data_structure_invariants: User-supplied blob data must be bounded at ingress by the maximum compliant blob size with an encoding-expansion allowance.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The report defines this as uint64(MaxSRSPoints * BytesPerSymbol / MaxCodingRatio); the encoded request-body cap should account for encoding inefficiency.
numeric_domains.name: MaxAllowedBlobSize

state_context.state_machine: HTTP blob submission reaches request-body consumption and blob encoding in the proxy handler.
